canonical_work.author: Masahiko Togawa
canonical_work.title: Eliade's Sojourn in India and the Megalithic Culture of Indigenous Indian Societies: From the Theory of Archaic Religion to Religions in the Human History
canonical_work.publisher_platform: J-STAGE / Japanese Association for Religious Studies
canonical_work.pdf_manifestation: publisher page exposes a 605K PDF download

scope_classification.scope_note: Publisher abstract explicitly states that the paper focuses on the Munda community of Jharkhand and uses a gravestone-consecration case. This does not justify generalization to all Munda communities or time periods.

deduplication.canonicalization_rule: DOI, J-STAGE article page, PDF, RIS/BibTeX and index records are manifestations/metadata of one canonical work and are not independent corroboration.
deduplication.independence_warning: Claims mediated through Eliade or other cited literature must retain dependency links and cannot be counted as independent primary evidence.

rights_access_cultural_governance.access_verified: J-STAGE labels article JOURNAL FREE ACCESS
rights_access_cultural_governance.copyright_notice: publisher page states © 2024 Japanese Association for Religious Studies
rights_access_cultural_governance.redistribution_permission: not established by free-access label alone
rights_access_cultural_governance.cultural_sensitivity: high for mortuary/gravestone consecration and sacred practice; exact passages require cultural-access review before public evidence promotion

required_before_claim_promotion: obtain publisher PDF lawfully and record cryptographic hash if repository storage is permitted
establish printed-page to PDF-page concordance for pp. 1-25
identify exact pages/sections for the Jharkhand Munda gravestone-consecration case
separate direct observation/field evidence, historical-source quotation, Eliade interpretation, author interpretation, and secondary citations
record locality, date, participant/source provenance and methodological basis where supplied
apply mortuary/sacred-practice cultural-access and consent/provenance review
promote only atomic propositions supported by exact locators and permitted evidence

promotion.reason: Identity, access and Munda-specific scope are verified, but proposition-level PDF locators, evidence dependencies, redistribution rights and cultural-governance review are not yet complete.

audit_principle: Discovery and free access do not equal evidence promotion or redistribution permission; unsupported cultural claims remain gaps.
